additions.site_name: Galaxy Backbone National Shared Services Centre (NSSC), Abuja
additions.name: Galaxy Backbone NSSC Abuja — existing Tier III data-centre operations (NSSC DC1)

status.summary: Galaxy Backbone's own post of 20 October 2026 names 'the Tier III National Shared Services Centre (NSSC) in Abuja' among its data centres and says Galaxy Backbone is the only public-sector organisation in Nigeria operating both Uptime Institute-certified Tier III and Tier IV data-centre infrastructure, providing hosting, cloud and co-location services. This records the NSSC Tier III data centre as operating on 20 October 2026, the post's publication day; it is not an opening date. Galaxy Backbone's 29 January 2025 release names the certified facility as NSSC DC1, Phase 1 (Uptime Tier III Certification of Constructed Facility); certification is context, not the status date, and no capacity is asserted.

locator.precision: Google's named 'Galaxy Backbone Limited, National Shared Services Center' marker, reached from the operator's own head-office map link, in the block north of Kur Mohammed Avenue and east of Ahmadu Bello Way, Central Business District, Abuja. It locates the NSSC campus, which the operator identifies as its corporate headquarters housing the Tier III data centre; it is not a data-hall location, building outline, parcel or boundary.
locator.identity_review: Galaxy Backbone's contact page links its head office (1243, Kur Mohammed Ave, Off Ahmadu Bello Way, Central Business District, Abuja; same address in its FAQ) to goo.gl/maps/uRf2zaRS569wq1Tv9, which resolves to the Google feature 'Galaxy Backbone Limited, National Shared Services Center' (0x104e0bb247a88c71:0x2dc5ae606be5343c); the point is that feature's place coordinate, not the map viewport. The head office is used only because the operator identifies it as the facility: its 14 April 2025 release calls the NSSC 'the organization's ultra-modern corporate headquarters' and records a tour there of 'the Uptime Certified Tier III Data Centre, Security Operations Centre, and Network Operations Centre', and its data-centre page says it operates the NSSC Tier III data centre as its primary data centre in the Federal Capital Territory. PeeringDB's self-reported 'Galaxy Backbone NSSC-Abuja' point (address '70, Kur Mohammed Avenue') lies 190 m to the south-west (pyproj WGS84 geodesic) and is kept as corroboration only. In Esri World Imagery (z18/z19, unknown date) the marker falls on open, partly worked ground inside the block, about 20-40 m from the nearest buildings, and Esri's street map labels Kur Mohammed Ave and Ahmadu Bello Way beside it; the imagery does not identify which building houses the data centre (geometry facts).
locator.uncertainty_reason: The map feature publishes no surveyed accuracy and the operator publishes no coordinate, plot number or boundary; the marker falls on open ground within the block rather than on an identified building, and PeeringDB's self-reported point is 190 m away.

additions.site_name: Galaxy Backbone National Tier IV Data Centre, Kano
additions.name: Galaxy Backbone Kano — existing Tier IV data-centre operations

status.summary: Galaxy Backbone's own post of 20 October 2026 names 'the Tier IV Data Centre in Kano' among its data centres and says Galaxy Backbone is the only public-sector organisation in Nigeria operating both Uptime Institute-certified Tier III and Tier IV data-centre infrastructure, providing hosting, cloud and co-location services. This records the Kano Tier IV data centre as operating on 20 October 2026, the post's publication day; it is not an opening date. The data centre was commissioned in February 2023 and certified Tier IV (design and facility) in 2024; both are historical context, and no capacity is asserted.

locator.precision: Google's named 'Galaxy Backbone LTD' marker, reached from the operator's own map link for its Kano office (Plot 2174, Ahmadu Bello Way, GRA Nassarawa), on the west side of Ahmadu Bello Way, Kano. It locates the operator's Kano compound, inferred to host the Tier IV data centre; it is not a data-hall location, building outline, parcel or boundary.
locator.identity_review: Galaxy Backbone's contact page lists one Kano address, 'Kano Office Plot 2174, Along Ahmadu Bello Way, GRA Nassarawa, Kano', linked to goo.gl/maps/3gTRqVE6BNqSUXVY7, which resolves to the Google feature 'Galaxy Backbone LTD' (0x11ae81d811e354ab:0x3528cba49751beb2); the point is that feature's place coordinate, not the map viewport. The data centre is placed at this compound by inference from the operator's own posts: on 20 February 2023 it thanked the minister for 'the successful commissioning of the National Tier IV data centre and North West Regional Office in Kano', and its 18 September 2024 account of a visit to 'its state-of-the-art Tier IV Data Centre in Kano' says the visitor toured key Galaxy Backbone facilities including the Network Operations Centre, conference room, training room and the Tier IV Data Centre. In Esri World Imagery (z18/z19, unknown date) the marker falls on a single-storey structure with rows of rooftop plant beside a larger white-roofed building in a walled compound fronting Ahmadu Bello Way (labelled on Esri's street map), consistent with an office compound hosting a modular data hall (the operator describes the Kano facility as a prefabricated modular data centre built with Huawei); the imagery does not confirm the data centre (geometry facts). PeeringDB lists no Galaxy Backbone facility in Kano.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The map feature publishes no surveyed accuracy; the operator publishes no coordinate, plot boundary or explicit statement that the Tier IV data centre stands at its Kano office, so the identity is inferred and the imagery check is qualitative, with unknown imagery date and accuracy.

additions.name: Teraco CT1 Rondebosch — existing data-centre operations
additions.site_identity_review: The Atlas site 'Teraco CT1 Data Centre' (vcc-site-2a7b2edfacb6958b2186) holds one project, the CT1 expansion (curated:teraco-ct1-rondebosch-data-centre:current-expansion), located by Teraco's printed CT1 GPS point -33.9712, 18.4649 from the CT1 tab of the same Cape Town locations page. The 28 September 2026 page version describes the operating CT1 facility at the Great Westerford Building, Rondebosch, and prints the identical 'GPS Co-ordinates: -33.971200, 18.464900', so the operating facility is the same physical site. Teraco's 12 November 2025 release separates the existing CT1 (2,500 square metres of data halls, 3 MW critical IT load) from the expansion of a further 1,000 square metres and 2 MW, which stays its own project with its own status.

status.summary: Teraco's Cape Town locations page, in its version modified on 28 September 2026, says Teraco operates vendor-neutral colocation data centres in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban and lists Rondebosch CT1 among its Cape Town facilities: Teraco's first vendor-neutral colocation facility, in the commercial heart of Rondebosch at the Great Westerford Building, with an interconnected ecosystem of more than 7,000 cross-connects and 100+ network service providers. This records the existing CT1 facility as operating on 28 September 2026, the modification day of the captured version (bounded by the Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026, which shows the same CT1 text in the 13 August version, and the live capture of 27 October 2026); it is not an opening date. The page's 2,500 sqm white space and IT load of 5 are facility specifications, not load in service, and the CT1 expansion (under construction, completion targeted for early 2027) is not part of this project.

locator.identity_review: Reuses the existing Teraco CT1 campus point exactly (-33.9712, 18.4649; Teraco's printed CT1 GPS point from the CT1 tab of its Cape Town locations page, evidence 3f9c9345-6060-57f1-af90-8f61f17e2cab), with no geometry-identity evidence rows. The 28 September 2026 page version and the 14 August 2026 archive copy print the same 'GPS Co-ordinates: -33.971200, 18.464900' for CT1, so the point still locates the CT1 facility; it is not a building outline or boundary and does not separate the existing halls from the expansion.
